news.title: All White Tommy Smith’s former club chase World Cup payments
news.lede: The owner of English club Braintree Town says football authorities owe them significant sums of money following former player Tommy Smith’s involvement in the FIFA Men’s World Cup. Braintree chairman Lee Harding has raised concerns about outstanding payments, according to a report in the Colchester Gazette. “Our club are still owed money, lots of it, hundreds of thousands of pounds, by The FA, UEFA and FIFA,” said Harding. The issue centres on money the National League club believe they are entitled to receive following Smith’s selection for New Zealand’s World Cup squad.

news.title: England’s Rugby Football League creates development panel after World Cup exit — BBC Sport
news.lede: England’s Rugby Football League (RFL) has announced the creation of the One Game, One England panel to prepare a plan for developing the game after England’s men’s and women’s teams failed to progress beyond the group stage of the Rugby League World Cup. Former Great Britain captain Paul Sculthorpe, retiring England women’s captain Jodie Cunningham and former international Adrian Morley will take part in its work, BBC Sport reports. England’s men’s team won two of their three group-stage matches and finished with a points difference of +86, but that was not enough to reach the play-offs. Their elimination was finally confirmed after Tonga defeated Samoa 20-18.

news.title: Football star Javi Martinez predicts a first class World Cup in Qatar
news.lede: BERLIN (Germany) - Spain's 2010 FIFA World Cup winner Javi Martinez spent nine successful years playing football for European giants Bayern Munich and developing a love for so many things in Germany. It was a no-brainer that he'd show up in Berlin when the city hosted the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup this summer. Martinez brought some good luck to Berlin because Spain ended up defeating Germany in the Third Place Game to reach the podium. It turns out he's also the ideal person to offer insight to another country, Qatar, which is hosting the FIBA Basketball World Cup next year.

news.title: Rugby Football League convenes panel to help fix national team after historically bad World Cup
news.lede: The RFL have convened a panel of former players to address the deep-rooted issues for the sport internationally after a worst-ever Rugby League World Cup performance. Both the men’s and women’s sides have crashed out of the Rugby League World Cup in the group stages, marking the worst-ever performance for England. The men won two of their three games but were unfortunate victims to the tournament’s format though many will rightfully argue that the best four nations have made the tournament’s semi-final stages anyway. With major changes need to ensure England do not get left behind on the international scene, the Rugby Football League (RFL) have shared a statement to confirm that they are launching a panel that will look to ‘map out a future for the national game’.
